title: Indifference opposed to necessity is of freedom's essence; indetermination implying potentiality is not
source_text: XV. Ad id vero quod objicitur praedeterminationem decreti divini ad hunc aut illum actum ex voluntate tollere indifferentiam ad operandum, in qua indifferentia posita est libertas: Respondet, Indifferentiam quae opponitur Determinationi ad unum ex necessitate, esse de essentia libertatis & hanc habere liberum arbitrium etiam in eo instanti, quo efficaciter praedeterminatur a Deo ad operandum; imo in ipso instanti quo operatur, non autem esse de essentia libertatis indeterminationem, ut importat potentialitatem, & privationem actus secundi, & ut opponitur determinationi ad alteram partem per modum libertatis, qui in facultate ad utrumlibet consistit.
pass_a_gloss: XV. But to that which is objected, that the predetermination of the divine decree to this or that act takes away from the will indifference to working, in which indifference freedom is placed: He answers, that Indifference which is opposed to Determination to one from necessity, is of the essence of freedom, and that free choice has this even in that instant in which it is efficaciously predetermined by God to work; nay, in the very instant in which it works; but that indetermination is not of the essence of freedom, as it imports potentiality, and privation of second act, and as it is opposed to determination to one part by way of freedom, which consists in a faculty for either.
pass_b_english: It is objected that the predetermination of the divine decree to this or that act takes from the will its indifference to acting, in which freedom lies. Alvarez answers that the indifference opposed to being determined to one thing by necessity does belong to the essence of freedom.

Free choice has this indifference even at the moment when God efficaciously predetermines it to act, indeed at the very moment it acts. What does not belong to the essence of freedom is indetermination in the sense that implies potentiality and the lack of a second act, and that is opposed to being determined to one side in the manner proper to freedom, which consists in a capacity for either side.

lemmas.gloss: as it imports potentiality, and privation of second act
consists in a faculty for either

choices.why: The will's openness to either alternative, in which many placed the essence of freedom; kept as the technical term.
